sanskrit: atha taṃ vyathayā dīnaṃ saviśeṣam amarṣitam śvasantam iva nāgendraṃ roṣavisphāritekṣaṇam
english: Then, seeing him afflicted with anguish, intensely indignant, breathing like a mighty serpent, his eyes dilated with fury —

sanskrit: āsādya rāmaḥ saumitriṃ suhṛdaṃ bhrātaraṃ priyam uvācedaṃ sa dhairyeṇa dhārayan sattvam ātmavān
english: — Rāma, self-possessed, steadying his composure with fortitude, approached Saumitri, that dear friend and beloved brother, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: saumitre yo 'bhiṣekārthe mama saṃbhārasaṃbhramaḥ abhiṣekanivṛttyarthe so 'stu saṃbhārasaṃbhramaḥ
english: "O Saumitri, let the bustle of preparations that was made for my consecration now serve instead for the reversal of that consecration.

sanskrit: yasyā madabhiṣekārthaṃ mānasaṃ paritapyate mātā naḥ sā yathā na syāt saviśaṅkā tathā kuru
english: She whose heart is being tormented on account of my consecration — that mother of ours — act in such a way that she may have no further cause for anxiety.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ śaṅkāmayaṃ duḥkhaṃ muhūrtam api notsahe manasi pratisaṃjātaṃ saumitre 'ham upekṣitum
english: I cannot bear, O Saumitri, to disregard even for a moment the grief born of apprehension that has arisen in her heart.

sanskrit: na buddhipūrvaṃ nābuddhaṃ smarāmīha kadā cana mātṝṇāṃ vā pitur vāhaṃ kṛtam alpaṃ ca vipriyam
english: I do not recall having ever done, intentionally or unwittingly, even the slightest thing displeasing to my mothers or to my father.

sanskrit: satyaḥ satyābhisaṃdhaś ca nityaṃ satyaparākramaḥ paralokabhayād bhīto nirbhayo 'stu pitā mama
english: My father, who is truthful, steadfast in his truth-pledges, ever of true valor — may he who fears the sin of falsehood in the next world be freed from fear.

sanskrit: tasyāpi hi bhaved asmin karmaṇy apratisaṃhṛte satyaṃ neti manastāpas tasya tāpas tapec ca mām
english: For if this act is not carried through, his heart would burn with the torment that his pledge of truth was not honored — and his torment would in turn torment me.

sanskrit: abhiṣekavidhānaṃ tu tasmāt saṃhṛtya lakṣmaṇa anvag evāham icchāmi vanaṃ gantum itaḥ punaḥ
english: Therefore, O Lakṣmaṇa, having set aside the rite of consecration, I wish straightaway to depart to the forest from this very place.

sanskrit: mama pravrājanād adya kṛtakṛtyā nṛpātmajā sutaṃ bharatam avyagram abhiṣecayitā tataḥ
english: Once I am banished today, that king's daughter will have achieved her purpose, and then she will consecrate her son Bharata without impediment.

sanskrit: mayi cīrājinadhare jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇi gate 'raṇyaṃ ca kaikeyyā bhaviṣyati manaḥsukham
english: When I have gone to the forest clad in bark garments and deerskin, wearing matted locks, Kaikeyī's heart will be at peace.

sanskrit: buddhiḥ praṇītā yeneyaṃ manaś ca susamāhitam tat tu nārhāmi saṃkleṣṭuṃ pravrajiṣyāmi māciram
english: That by which this resolve has been directed and the mind fully composed — that I ought not to trouble; I shall go forth without delay.

sanskrit: kṛtāntas tv eva saumitre draṣṭavyo matpravāsane rājyasya ca vitīrṇasya punar eva nivartane
english: In my banishment and in the return of the kingdom that was granted to me — fate alone, O Saumitri, is to be seen at work.

sanskrit: kaikeyyāḥ pratipattir hi kathaṃ syān mama pīḍane yadi bhāvo na daivo 'yaṃ kṛtāntavihito bhavet
english: For how could Kaikeyī have come to act in such a way as to cause me harm, were this not the disposition of fate, ordained by the god of death?

sanskrit: jānāsi hi yathā saumya na mātṛṣu mamāntaram bhūtapūrvaṃ viśeṣo vā tasyā mayi sute 'pi vā
english: For you know, O gentle one, that there was never any distinction in my regard for my mothers, nor any special difference in hers toward me, her child.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣekanivṛttyarthaiḥ pravāsārthaiś ca durvacaiḥ ugrair vākyair ahaṃ tasyā nānyad daivāt samarthaye
english: Therefore, that she should have spoken to me those harsh, bitter words aimed at annulling the consecration and at banishment — I attribute this to nothing other than fate.

sanskrit: kathaṃ prakṛtisaṃpannā rājaputrī tathāguṇā brūyāt sā prākṛteva strī matpīḍāṃ bhartṛsaṃnidhau
english: How could a princess of such natural nobility, possessed of such qualities, have spoken in the presence of her husband of my humiliation, as though she were a common woman?

sanskrit: yad acintyaṃ tu tad daivaṃ bhūteṣv api na hanyate vyaktaṃ mayi ca tasyāṃ ca patito hi viparyayaḥ
english: That fate which is inscrutable cannot be prevented even among living beings — clearly, a reversal has befallen both her and me.

sanskrit: kaś cid daivena saumitre yoddhum utsahate pumān yasya na grahaṇaṃ kiṃ cit karmaṇo 'nyatra dṛśyate
english: Who, O Saumitri, can venture to fight against fate, whose workings in any action can be grasped by nothing other than itself?

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe bhayakrodhau lābhālābhau bhavābhavau yasya kiṃ cit tathābhūtaṃ nanu daivasya karma tat
english: Pleasure and pain, fear and anger, gain and loss, existence and non-existence — whatever is thus constituted, is that not indeed the work of fate?

sanskrit: vyāhate 'py abhiṣeke me paritāpo na vidyate tasmād aparitāpaḥ saṃs tvam apy anuvidhāya mām pratisaṃhāraya kṣipram ābhiṣecanikīṃ kriyām
english: Even though my consecration has been thwarted, I feel no grief. Therefore, free from grief yourself and following my lead, quickly withdraw the preparations for the consecration rite.

sanskrit: na lakṣmaṇāsmin mama rājyavighne mātā yavīyasy atiśaṅkanīyā daivābhipannā hi vadanty aniṣṭaṃ jānāsi daivaṃ ca tathāprabhāvam
english: O Lakṣmaṇa, in this obstruction of my kingship, the younger mother is not to be overly blamed — for those overtaken by fate speak of unwished things; and you know well the power of fate to work thus.

sanskrit: iti bruvati rāme tu lakṣmaṇo 'dhaḥśirā muhuḥ śrutvā madhyaṃ jagāmeva manasā duḥkhaharṣayoḥ
english: While Rāma was speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa repeatedly hung his head low; hearing these words, he felt himself pulled between grief and fierce resolve.

sanskrit: tadā tu baddhvā bhrukuṭīṃ bhruvor madhye nararṣabha niśaśvāsa mahāsarpo bilastha iva roṣitaḥ
english: Then, O bull among men, he knitted his brows together, and breathed hard — like a great serpent coiled in its den, enraged.

sanskrit: tasya duṣprativīkṣyaṃ tad bhrukuṭīsahitaṃ tadā babhau kruddhasya siṃhasya mukhasya sadṛśaṃ mukham
english: His face, set with that fearsome frown, was then unbearable to behold — resembling the visage of a lion roused to wrath.

sanskrit: agrahas taṃ vidhunvaṃs tu hastī hastam ivātmanaḥ tiryag ūrdhvaṃ śarīre ca pātayitvā śirodharām
english: He who was unconstrained, shaking like an elephant shaking its own trunk, let his neck drop sideways and upward across his body —

sanskrit: agrākṣṇā vīkṣamāṇas tu tiryag bhrātaram abravīt asthāne saṃbhramo yasya jāto vai sumahān ayam
english: — and looking at his brother askance from the corners of his eyes, he said: "This very great agitation of yours has arisen in the wrong place.

sanskrit: dharmadoṣaprasaṅgena lokasyānatiśaṅkayā kathaṃ hy etad asaṃbhrāntas tvadvidho vaktum arhati
english: How could a man of your stature speak such things composedly, when the world would not so readily suspect fault in dharma?

sanskrit: yathā daivam aśauṇḍīraṃ śauṇḍīraḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ kiṃ nāma kṛpaṇaṃ daivam aśaktam abhiśaṃsasi
english: Why do you, a bold bull among kṣatriyas, praise fate as though it were cowardly? Why do you invoke pitiful, impotent fate?

sanskrit: pāpayos te kathaṃ nāma tayoḥ śaṅkā na vidyate santi dharmopadhāḥ ślakṣṇā dharmātman kiṃ na budhyase
english: O righteous one, how is it that you harbor no suspicion of those two sinful ones? There are subtle tests of dharma — do you not perceive them?

sanskrit: lokavidviṣṭam ārabdhaṃ tvadanyasyābhiṣecanam yeneyam āgatā dvaidhaṃ tava buddhir mahīpate sa hi dharmo mama dveṣyaḥ prasaṅgād yasya muhyasi
english: The consecration of another in your place — which the world would hate — is what has led your mind to this confusion, O lord of the earth. That very dharma by whose invocation you are bewildered is hateful to me.

sanskrit: yady api pratipattis te daivī cāpi tayor matam tathāpy upekṣaṇīyaṃ te na me tad api rocate
english: Even if your resolve is of divine origin and their opinion carries weight, still, the fact that you would overlook this — that does not please me either.

sanskrit: viklavo vīryahīno yaḥ sa daivam anuvartate vīrāḥ saṃbhāvitātmāno na daivaṃ paryupāsate
english: One who is faint-hearted and bereft of valor submits to fate; heroes who hold their souls in high esteem do not merely worship fate.

sanskrit: daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa yaḥ samarthaḥ prabādhitum na daivena vipannārthaḥ puruṣaḥ so 'vasīdati
english: A man who has the power to overcome fate by his own exertion does not sink down when his purpose is ruined by fate.

sanskrit: drakṣyanti tv adya daivasya pauruṣaṃ puruṣasya ca daivamānuṣayor adya vyaktā vyaktir bhaviṣyati
english: Today they shall see the power of fate and the power of a man; today the distinction between the divine and the human will be made manifest.

sanskrit: adya matpauruṣahataṃ daivaṃ drakṣyanti vai janāḥ yad daivād āhataṃ te 'dya dṛṣṭaṃ rājyābhiṣecanam
english: Today people shall see fate struck down by my valor, just as today we have seen your royal consecration struck down by fate.

sanskrit: atyaṅkuśam ivoddāmaṃ gajaṃ madabaloddhatam pradhāvitam ahaṃ daivaṃ pauruṣeṇa nivartaye
english: Just as a maddened elephant running rampant beyond the goad is turned back, so I shall turn back fate by my own exertion.

sanskrit: lokapālāḥ samastās te nādya rāmābhiṣecanam na ca kṛtsnās trayo lokā vihanyuḥ kiṃ punaḥ pitā
english: Not all the guardians of the worlds together could obstruct Rāma's consecration today — nor could all three worlds — much less a father alone.

sanskrit: yair vivāsas tavāraṇye mitho rājan samarthitaḥ araṇye te vivatsyanti caturdaśa samās tathā
english: Those who have secretly conspired for your exile to the forest, O king — they shall dwell in the forest likewise for fourteen years.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tadāśāṃ chetsyāmi pitus tasyāś ca yā tava abhiṣekavighātena putrarājyāya vartate
english: I shall cut off that hope of your father and of her — the hope that works through obstructing your consecration so that a son may become king.

sanskrit: madbalena viruddhāya na syād daivabalaṃ tathā prabhaviṣyati duḥkhāya yathograṃ pauruṣaṃ mama
english: Faced with my power in opposition, the force of fate shall not be able to prevail to cause harm in the way my own fierce exertion shall.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ varṣasahasrānte prajāpālyam anantaram āryaputrāḥ kariṣyanti vanavāsaṃ gate tvayi
english: After a thousand years, once the duty of ruling over the people is fulfilled, the noble-born sons shall perform the forest-dwelling themselves — after you have already gone.

sanskrit: pūrvarājarṣivṛttyā hi vanavāso vidhīyate prajā nikṣipya putreṣu putravat paripālane
english: For according to the way of former royal seers, forest-dwelling is prescribed — entrusting the people to one's sons to be cared for as children.

sanskrit: sa ced rājany anekāgre rājyavibhramaśaṅkayā naivam icchasi dharmātman rājyaṃ rāma tvam ātmani
english: O king, if out of fear that the kingship might be disrupted by a divided mind you do not wish to hold the kingdom in yourself, O Rāma, O righteous one —

sanskrit: pratijāne ca te vīra mā bhūvaṃ vīralokabhāk rājyaṃ ca tava rakṣeyam ahaṃ veleva sāgaram
english: — then I pledge to you, O hero — may I forfeit my place in the world of heroes — I shall guard your kingdom as the shore guards the ocean.

sanskrit: maṅgalair abhiṣiñcasva tatra tvaṃ vyāpṛto bhava aham eko mahīpālān alaṃ vārayituṃ balāt
english: Be consecrated with auspicious rites; be engaged in that alone. I alone am capable of holding back by force all the kings of the earth.

sanskrit: na śobhārthāv imau bāhū na dhanur bhūṣaṇāya me nāsirābandhanārthāya na śarāḥ stambhahetavaḥ
english: These two arms of mine are not for adornment; the bow is not worn by me for decoration; the sword is not bound on for show; the arrows are not for display.

sanskrit: amitradamanārthaṃ me sarvam etac catuṣṭayam na cāhaṃ kāmaye 'tyarthaṃ yaḥ syāc chatrur mato mama
english: All these four — arms, bow, sword, and arrows — serve me for the crushing of enemies; nor do I have excessive desire for what I regard as hostile.

sanskrit: asinā tīkṣṇadhāreṇa vidyuccalitavarcasā pragṛhītena vai śatruṃ vajriṇaṃ vā na kalpaye
english: With my sharp-edged sword, blazing like leaping lightning, I count as no foe even the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.

sanskrit: khaḍganiṣpeṣaniṣpiṣṭair gahanā duścarā ca me hastyaśvanarahastoruśirobhir bhavitā mahī
english: The ground before me, dense and hard to traverse, shall be strewn with the trunks, thighs, and heads of elephants, horses, and men — crushed and pressed by my sword's blows.

sanskrit: khaḍgadhārāhatā me 'dya dīpyamānā ivādrayaḥ patiṣyanti dvipā bhūmau meghā iva savidyutaḥ
english: Today, struck by my sword's edge, elephants shall fall to earth blazing like mountains — like clouds falling with their lightning.

sanskrit: baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇe pragṛhītaśarāsane kathaṃ puruṣamānī syāt puruṣāṇāṃ mayi sthite
english: With my leather finger-guard strapped on and my bow taken up, how could anyone count himself a true man among men while I yet stand?

sanskrit: bahubhiś caikam atyasyann ekena ca bahūñ janān viniyokṣyāmy ahaṃ bāṇān nṛvājigajamarmasu
english: Surpassing many enemies as one, and many as if they were one, I shall release my arrows into the vital points of men, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: adya me 'straprabhāvasya prabhāvaḥ prabhaviṣyati rājñaś cāprabhutāṃ kartuṃ prabhutvaṃ ca tava prabho
english: Today the power of my weapons shall make itself felt — to strip the king of his sovereignty and to establish your sovereignty, O master.

sanskrit: adya candanasārasya keyūrāmokṣaṇasya ca vasūnāṃ ca vimokṣasya suhṛdāṃ pālanasya ca
english: Today — for the sake of sandalwood paste and the loosening of armlets, for the bestowal of wealth, and for the protection of friends —

sanskrit: anurūpāv imau bāhū rāma karma kariṣyataḥ abhiṣecanavighnasya kartṝṇāṃ te nivāraṇe
english: — these two arms of mine shall do fitting work, O Rāma, in warding off those who are responsible for the obstruction of your consecration.

sanskrit: bravīhi ko 'dyaiva mayā viyujyatāṃ tavāsuhṛt prāṇayaśaḥ suhṛjjanaiḥ yathā taveyaṃ vasudhā vaśe bhavet tathaiva māṃ śādhi tavāsmi kiṃkaraḥ
english: Tell me — who is your enemy, that he may this very day be separated from me, from life and glory? Command me as you see fit so that this earth may come under your sway; I am your servant.

sanskrit: vimṛjya bāṣpaṃ parisāntvya cāsakṛt sa lakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavavaṃśavardhanaḥ uvāca pitrye vacane vyavasthitaṃ nibodha mām eṣa hi saumya satpathaḥ
english: Wiping away his tears and consoling Lakṣmaṇa again and again, he who was the enhancer of the Rāghava line said: "Know me as one firmly set in our father's command — this, O gentle Saumitri, is the true path."

sanskrit: taṃ samīkṣya tv avahitaṃ pitur nirdeśapālane kausalyā bāṣpasaṃruddhā vaco dharmiṣṭham abravīt
english: Seeing him steadfastly intent on fulfilling his father's decree, Kausalyā, choking with tears, spoke righteous words.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭaduḥkho dharmātmā sarvabhūtapriyaṃvadaḥ mayi jāto daśarathāt katham uñchena vartayet
english: "One who has never known sorrow, righteous in soul, beloved in speech to all living beings — born of Daśaratha and of me — how shall he live by gleaning?

sanskrit: yasya bhṛtyāś ca dāsāś ca mṛṣṭāny annāni bhuñjate kathaṃ sa bhokṣyate nātho vane mūlaphalāny ayam
english: He whose own servants and slaves eat the finest prepared food — how shall that lord subsist in the forest on roots and fruits?

sanskrit: ka etac chraddadhec chrutvā kasya vā na bhaved bhayam guṇavān dayito rājño rāghavo yad vivāsyate
english: Who would believe this, hearing it? And for whom would fear not arise — that Rāghava, virtuous and beloved of the king, is being banished?

sanskrit: tvayā vihīnām iha māṃ śokāgnir atulo mahān pradhakṣyati yathā kakṣaṃ citrabhānur himātyaye
english: Bereft of you, the immeasurable great fire of grief shall consume me, as the bright-flamed fire consumes dry grass at the end of winter.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi dhenuḥ svaṃ vatsaṃ gacchantaṃ nānugacchati ahaṃ tvānugamiṣyāmi yatra putra gamiṣyasi
english: For how could a cow not follow her own calf when it departs? I shall follow you, O son, wherever you go.

sanskrit: tathā nigaditaṃ mātrā tad vākyaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ śrutvā rāmo 'bravīd vākyaṃ mātaraṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitām
english: Having heard those words spoken thus by his mother, Rāma, that bull among men, spoke in reply to his deeply grieved mother:

sanskrit: kaikeyyā vañcito rājā mayi cāraṇyam āśrite bhavatyā ca parityakto na nūnaṃ vartayiṣyati
english: "Deceived by Kaikeyī, and with me gone to the forest, and abandoned by you as well, the king surely will not survive.

sanskrit: bhartuḥ kila parityāgo nṛśaṃsaḥ kevalaṃ striyāḥ sa bhavatyā na kartavyo manasāpi vigarhitaḥ
english: The abandonment of one's husband is said to be a cruelty peculiar to a woman — that you must not do, condemned even in thought.

sanskrit: yāvaj jīvati kākutsthaḥ pitā me jagatīpatiḥ śuśrūṣā kriyatāṃ tāvat sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: As long as my father, the Kākutstha, lord of the earth, still lives — serve him; that is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: evam uktā tu rāmeṇa kausalyā śubha darśanā tathety uvāca suprītā rāmam akliṣṭakāriṇam
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the fair-visaged Kausalyā replied "So be it" with full willingness to Rāma the tireless in action.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vacanaṃ rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ bhūyas tām abravīd vākyaṃ mātaraṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitām
english: Thus addressed, Rāma, foremost among the upholders of dharma, once more spoke these words to his deeply grieved mother:

sanskrit: mayā caiva bhavatyā ca kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ rājā bhartā guruḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarveṣām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
english: "Both you and I must do our father's bidding — the king is husband, teacher, most excellent, the lord and master of all.

sanskrit: imāni tu mahāraṇye vihṛtya nava pañca ca varṣāṇi paramaprītaḥ sthāsyāmi vacane tava
english: Having passed these fourteen years in the great forest, I shall return in supreme gladness and shall abide by your word.

sanskrit: evam uktā priyaṃ putraṃ bāṣpapūrṇānanā tadā uvāca paramārtā tu kausalyā putravatsalā
english: Thus addressed, her face filled with tears, her heart consumed with anguish, Kausalyā, that devoted mother, then spoke to her beloved son:

sanskrit: āsāṃ rāma sapatnīnāṃ vastuṃ madhye na me kṣamam naya mām api kākutstha vanaṃ vanyaṃ mṛgīṃ yathā yadi te gamane buddhiḥ kṛtā pitur apekṣayā
english: "It is not possible for me to dwell among these co-wives, O Rāma. Take me too, O Kākutstha, to the forest, like a doe of the wild — if your mind is resolved on going, in deference to your father.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā rudatīṃ rāmo rudan vacanam abravīt jīvantyā hi striyā bhartā daivataṃ prabhur eva ca bhavatyā mama caivādya rājā prabhavati prabhuḥ
english: To her weeping thus, Rāma, himself in tears, replied: "For a living woman, her husband is the deity and the master — today the king is master, lord over both you and me.

sanskrit: bharataś cāpi dharmātmā sarvabhūtapriyaṃvadaḥ bhavatīm anuvarteta sa hi dharmarataḥ sadā
english: And Bharata too, righteous in soul, dear in speech to all creatures, will attend to you — for he is always devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: yathā mayi tu niṣkrānte putraśokena pārthivaḥ śramaṃ nāvāpnuyāt kiṃ cid apramattā tathā kuru
english: Act vigilantly so that, after my departure, the king may not suffer even the slightest affliction through grief for his son.

sanskrit: vratopavāsaniratā yā nārī paramottamā bhartāraṃ nānuvarteta sā ca pāpagatir bhavet
english: A woman, however supremely excellent, who is devoted to vows and fasts but does not follow her husband's path — even she incurs a sinful fate.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣam eva kurvīta bhartuḥ priyahite ratā eṣa dharmaḥ purā dṛṣṭo loke vede śrutaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: She should render service alone, devoted to the beloved welfare of her husband — this is the dharma seen of old in the world, heard in the Veda, and remembered in the Smṛtis.

sanskrit: pūjyās te matkṛte devi brāhmaṇāś caiva suvratāḥ evaṃ kālaṃ pratīkṣasva mamāgamanakāṅkṣiṇī
english: O queen, on my account you should honor the brāhmaṇas and those of excellent vows — and thus wait out the time, longing for my return.

sanskrit: prāpsyase paramaṃ kāmaṃ mayi pratyāgate sati yadi dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho dhārayiṣyati jīvitam
english: You shall attain your supreme wish when I return — if the foremost of those who uphold dharma, the king, shall hold on to life.

sanskrit: evam uktā tu rāmeṇa bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā kausalyā putraśokārtā rāmaṃ vacanam abravīt gaccha putra tvam ekāgro bhadraṃ te 'stu sadā vibho
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, her eyes clouded with a rush of tears, Kausalyā, afflicted by the sorrow for her son, spoke to Rāma: "Go, my son, single-minded; may you ever be blessed, O lord."

sanskrit: tathā hi rāmaṃ vanavāsaniścitaṃ samīkṣya devī parameṇa cetasā uvāca rāmaṃ śubhalakṣaṇaṃ vaco babhūva ca svastyayanābhikāṅkṣiṇī
english: Thus indeed, seeing Rāma resolved upon forest-dwelling, the queen with her highest mind spoke words to Rāma of auspicious marks, and she became one who longed to perform rites of benediction over him.
